name: IPO base
shape: A recent listing building its first real base, holding above its 50-day line.
description: This screen looks for a company that listed recently and is building its first proper base. There is no relative strength dial on this screen at all — a young listing has not been trading long enough for a twelve-month ranking to mean anything, and we would rather show you nothing than a number we made up.

concepts.title: Recently listed
concepts.text: The company has been public for under a year. There is no RS dial on this screen, because a young listing has not had the twelve months relative strength needs.

concepts.title: Its first real base
concepts.text: Its first stretch of weeks going sideways instead of up.

concepts.title: Holding its 50-day line
concepts.text: It is staying above its short trend line while it rests.

concepts.title: The pivot
concepts.text: The top of that first base.

concepts.title: Breakout
concepts.text: A close above the top of the first base.

concepts.title: Climbing
concepts.text: It cleared the pivot earlier and is still above its trailing line.

funnel.title: The liquid US universe
funnel.text: US common stocks over $5, market cap over $300M, and at least $5M traded a day over the last 20 sessions.

funnel.title: Recently listed
funnel.text: On the market for less than 50 weeks.

funnel.title: Where we look for the ceiling
funnel.text: The pivot is the highest price of the last 26 weeks.

funnel.title: Long enough to be a base
funnel.text: The base has lasted at least 3 weeks.

funnel.title: Not a collapse
funnel.text: From its ceiling, the base never fell more than 35%.

funnel.title: Holding its 50-day line
funnel.text: Price is above the average of the last 50 days.

funnel.title: Near the trigger
funnel.text: Price is no more than 20% below the pivot.

funnel_preface: Every number below is a dial you can move in Filters.

params.label: Longest since listing we'll accept
params.funnel_text: On the market for less than {value} weeks.
params.help: Measured from the listing date, or from the first session we hold for the stock.

params.label: How far back to look for the ceiling
params.funnel_title: Where we look for the ceiling
params.funnel_text: The pivot is the highest price of the last {value} weeks.
params.help: The window we search for the price the stock has to clear. A longer window finds older, larger structures.

params.label: Shortest base we'll accept
params.funnel_title: Long enough to be a base
params.funnel_text: The base has lasted at least {value} weeks.
params.help: How long the stock has been going sideways. Shorter stretches are noise rather than structure.

params.label: Deepest base we'll accept
params.funnel_text: From its ceiling, the base never fell more than {value}%.
params.help: How far price dropped inside the base, measured from the ceiling to the lowest point. Deeper structures take longer to repair.

params.label: Must be above its 50-day line
params.funnel_text: Price is above the average of the last 50 days.
params.help: The average closing price of the last 50 sessions. For a young listing this is the only trend line with enough history to mean anything.

params.label: How far below the pivot we still list it
params.funnel_text: Price is no more than {value}% below the pivot.
params.help: How close the stock currently sits to the price it has to clear.

params.label: Smallest swing that counts as a contraction
params.help: A move smaller than this is treated as noise rather than as a pullback, so the contraction list stays readable.

params.label: How recent counts as fresh
params.help: A breakout stays in the fresh bucket for this many sessions before it moves to climbing.

params.label: Moving averages that must be in order
params.funnel_text: At least {value} of the three rungs hold — 9 above 21, 21 above 50, 50 above 200.
params.help: The 9, 21, 50 and 200-day averages, fastest to slowest. Three of three is a full stack: every timeframe pointing the same way. Zero turns this off, which is where it starts, so no screen changes until you move it. A stock with under 200 sessions of history has no 200-day average and is not judged on this at all.

trade_steps.title: Buy the breakout
trade_steps.text: As it pushes through the pivot.

trade_steps.title: Set a safety net
trade_steps.text: An automatic exit if it drops about 8% from where you got in.

trade_steps.title: Lock in "no loss"
trade_steps.text: Once it is up enough, move that net to where you started.

trade_steps.title: Ride the trend
trade_steps.text: Raise the net as it climbs.

trade_steps_preface: Risk is decided before entry — about 1.5% of capital on any one trade.
